bio.summary: Martus is a first-time council candidate and a senior adviser with a background in institutional finance. He emphasizes budget oversight, government trust and changes to land-use regulation.

statements.text: I support the continued operation of the airport and the acceptance of FAA funding.
statements.speaker: David Martus

statements.text: In general, I do not believe fragmenting the city into siloed revenue sources and spending pools is the best approach.
statements.speaker: David Martus

statements.text: I support the fundamental mission of a DDA, but the lack of detailed coordination with impacted agencies would have led me to vote no as well.
statements.speaker: David Martus
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — David Martus

statements.text: David Martus is a first-time candidate for Boulder City Council, running on a platform of fiscal stewardship, increasing trust in government and reducing regulation and bureaucracy.
statements.speaker: Boulder Reporting Lab reporter

statements.text: I believe the city’s current top three priorities are: 1) long-term financial stability; 2) wildfire and public-safety resilience; and 3) housing policy.
statements.speaker: David Martus

statements.text: I spent 25 years in institutional finance building consensus among people with different views, and I would bring that same approach to Council: listen first, be clear about facts and tradeoffs, and work toward practical agreement.
statements.speaker: David Martus
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — David Martus

statements.text: No. If higher density is part of the solution, I believe it should be focused in areas of the city that provide more benefits.
statements.speaker: David Martus

statements.text: Businesses should be able to expect a public safety presence to match their operating hours.
statements.speaker: David Martus
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — David Martus

statements.text: Yes. The build-out should proceed if the outcome is positive, the cost is reasonable, and lessons from completed projects are incorporated.
